title: Serveflow synchronizer: repair uneven TTFT across hosted/dedicated/private
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Over the last 48 hours multiple high-usage customers reported divergent TTFT and sustained tokens/sec degradation in EU and APAC regions. Impact spans Hosted API, Dedicated pools with burst enabled, and select Private clusters running the 1.25 kernel selector rollout. Symptoms: extended first-token latency (TTFT) for ~5-12% of requests, token emission slowdowns (tokens/sec drop by 20-40%) on models with long prompt priming, and a high variance tail observed on multiplexed sessions. This ticket coordinates triage, short-term mitigation and the production fix for the Serveflow synchronizer/reservation heuristic that interacts badly with the new heterogeneous kernel selection path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send mixed-size priming requests (200-2000 tokens) to a single tenant with multiplexing enabled and KV-prefetch enabled
2) Observe that under sustained fanout (50-200 req/s per tenant) some workers show delayed priming and low tokens/sec even when GPU utilization is nominal
3) Reproduce most reliably when kernel-selector variant "hetero-v2" is enabled and prefetch window is set to "auto"
4) Verify by toggling tenant-level prefetchoff flag and/or forcing kernel-selector to "homogeneous" to see immediate partial recovery
investigation_notes: Telemetry: spike in prefetch miss rate correlated with TTFT spikes. Trace samples show a pattern: prefetch enqueue -> allocation decision -> kernel mismatch fallback -> eviction of warm KV leading to priming re-issue.

Root cause hypothesis: the Serveflow synchronizer applies a variable prefetch reservation per-request based on recent token-rate heuristics. With hetero-v2 kernel selection the reservation calculation can return inconsistent sizes across the fanout path causing transient overcommit on a subset of worker queues and a cascade of KV evictions that prolong priming for in-flight requests.
Two customers escalated with reproducible traces (Customer A EU-prod, Customer B Private-onprem). Both traces show the eviction cascade and repeated priming attempts in the worker logs.
Related to recent rollout: kernel-selector hetero-v2 flagged in runtime-1.25. Telemetry shows the regression onset aligned with hetero-v2 rollouts in EU region on 2026-03-11.

Quant: affected requests ~7% of total across impacted tenants; for those requests median TTFT increases from 85ms to 380ms and 95th percentile to >1.2s. tokens/sec drops 20-40% for long outputs until manual intervention.
Risk assessment: high customer-visible latency and degraded throughput for certain workloads; urgent fix required before broader runtime-1.26 rollout.
decision_log: 2026-03-13 09:15 - Triage call: short-term mitigation approved: introduce tenant-prefetchoff flag and emergency rollback of hetero-v2 to homogenous for affected clusters.

2026-03-13 12:40 - Engineering decision: implement a deterministic reservation cap in Serveflow synchronizer (max_reservation_tokens default 256) to prevent overcommit; add metric for reservation_gap to detect mismatches.
2026-03-14 18:05 - Product/Support decision: customer bridge opened; customers A and B notified of mitigation plan and ETA for full fix.
actions: Mitigation (done): deploy tenant-level "prefetchoff" toggle and push config to affected EU/Dedicated/Private clusters (rolled out 2026-03-13 14:30 UTC). Observed immediate TTFT partial recovery for escalations.

Emergency rollback (done): revert kernel-selector hetero-v2 on EU-hosted and selected Dedicated pools (rolled back 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC). This step removed the largest regression vector but does not address internal reservation logic.
Code fix (in progress): implement deterministic reservation cap and normalization across the fanout path with unit tests and an integration test exercising mixed priming sizes under hetero kernels.
Observability (in progress): add reservation_gap, prefetch_miss_reason, and eviction_cascade_count traces. Create Alert: reservation_gap > 64 tokens for 5m in a tenant -> pager.

Postmortem actions (planned): extend pre-release rollout checklist to include cross-variant reservation-consistency test; schedule canary bursts for kernel selector changes; add runbook section for prefetchoff and kernel rollback.
observability: New metrics to add: reservation_gap, prefetch_miss_reason (enum), eviction_cascade_count
Dashboards to update: per-tenant TTFT heatmap, kernel-variant fanout map, eviction cascade scatterplot
Alerting: reservation_gap > 64 for 5m, prefetch_miss_rate > 5% sustained for 10m
postmortem_action_items: 1) Extend canary test harness to include hetero kernel permutations and variable priming sizes
2) Add deterministic-contract tests for reservation sizing across fanout path
3) Ship telemetry to detect reservation-inconsistency before user-visible impact
4) Update rollout checklist to require cross-deployment warmup and burst tests
5) Schedule follow-up audit of other heuristics that compute per-request resource reservations
